RESP-SHORT-1.description: [RESP-SHORT-1] The HEIGHT axis for core/ui/breakpoints.dart, and the first three call sites to use it. Every threshold in that file keyed off WIDTH, so the tester's BlackBerry-style QWERTY handset (KEYone/KEY2 class, ~393 x 590dp: normal width, two-thirds the usual height, hardware keyboard below the display) classified `regular`, took the full 1.22 type bump and got chromeScale 1.0 — [RESP-SMALL-1] and [RESP-SMALL-2] gave it exactly zero relief. NEW API, thresholds shortMax=640 / xshortMax=520 as proposed by Specs/AUDIT-SHORT-SCREEN-2026-08-21.md and adopted unchanged: isShort(context), heroHeightFraction(context) (1.0 / 0.42 / 0.34), chromeScaleHV(context) = min(chromeScale, vertical 1.0/0.85/0.72), each with a pure `*For`/`*Height` twin taking a raw double so the tiers are testable without pumping a widget. NO new ZineWidthClass variant and no ZineHeightClass enum — that enum is exhaustively switched at ~20 call sites and with no local Dart compiler a new variant is ~20 CI errors 40-80 minutes later; the helpers read the size directly, exactly as chromeScale does. Height NEVER scales type (main.dart's builder owns text scale once, app-wide; multiplying compounds into unreadable text on the very device this helps) and NEVER shrinks tap targets. chromeScaleHV is a NEW NAME, not a redefinition of chromeScale, so no existing caller changes behaviour. KEYBOARD DECISION: all helpers read the RAW MediaQuery.sizeOf().height, not height-minus-viewInsets — subtracting insets would make an ordinary 852dp phone read 552dp (i.e. `short`) the instant a keyboard rose and flip tiers back on dismiss, a visible layout jump on the majority of phones; a caller that needs remaining space must subtract viewInsets itself and clamp at 0. CONSUMERS (audit findings 5/6/7): (5) call_hero_composition.dart capped the width-derived hero height, 350dp = 59% of a 590dp viewport, at heroHeightFraction x viewport with width re-derived so the artwork keeps its aspect ratio — ~248dp on the tester's phone, unchanged at 350dp on a normal one; (6) ZineAppBar gained an OPTIONAL heightScale (default 1.0, so all ~45 existing call sites are unchanged) floored at 62dp so the 40dp back button plus its 8/12 padding cannot overflow the band, wired at the two hosts the audit named, inbox_list_screen.dart and marketplace_browse.dart; (7) RichPickerPanel's height is capped at 45% of the viewport in rich_input_bar.dart — its 300dp default is learned from the SOFT keyboard, which a hardware-keyboard phone may never raise, and 0.45 x 852 = 383 so the cap never binds on a normal phone. Findings 1-4 were fixed structurally in e44eb652 and are untouched. Client-only: no worker change, no schema change, no new flag, no new event.
RESP-SHORT-1.no_telemetry: Pure geometry plus a utility class. Nothing here emits, gates or branches on a server value: three tier functions, one height clamp on an SVG composition, one optional constructor arg on a header, one min() on a panel height. There is no property whose value could be read back to prove it, and inventing an event to satisfy the gate would be worse than saying so. NOTE ON WHAT IS ALREADY FILTERABLE: the `screen_metrics` event carries `height_dp` (main.dart:363) alongside the `width_class` [RESP-SMALL-1] put on the envelope, so a short device CAN be found in PostHog today with `screen_metrics where height_dp < 640`. Adding a `height_class` string to the envelope so EVERY event from a short device is filterable was considered and deliberately deferred: it needs a 3-line change in main.dart (the only place that has both the height and the emit), which was outside this task's file set. It is the obvious next increment and would turn this hatch into a real assertion. CONCRETE VISUAL CHECK meanwhile, on the tester's QWERTY phone or a 393x590 emulator profile, and a 393x852 control phone for the guardrail: (a) SHORT DEVICE, place an outgoing call and let it ring — the bell/petal/orbit hero must occupy roughly the TOP 40% of the screen, not 60%, the peer's name must be legible above it, and the photo must still sit centred in the dotted orbit; (b) CONTROL PHONE, same screen must look EXACTLY as it did before this change — if the hero shrank on an ordinary handset, heroHeightFraction is binding where it must not and the owner's signed-off design has regressed; (c) SHORT DEVICE, open Inbox and Marketplace (pushed, not embedded) — the indigo header band is visibly slimmer, the back arrow and title are fully inside it, and there is NO red overflow stripe (the 62dp floor is what prevents that; a stripe here means the floor is too low); (d) CONTROL PHONE, the same two headers must be unchanged at 76dp; (e) SHORT DEVICE, open a chat and tap the emoji button — the picker panel must stop at under half the screen with a usable strip of message list still visible above the composer; (f) CONTROL PHONE, the emoji panel must still open at exactly the remembered keyboard height, i.e. unchanged. The unit test app/test/ui/short_screen_breakpoints_test.dart pins the tier arithmetic itself, including the 'must not bind on an ordinary phone' guardrail, and CI runs it.

RESP-SMALL-3.description: [RESP-SMALL-3] Short-screen audit of the 2026-08-21 UI redesign (Specs/AUDIT-SHORT-SCREEN-2026-08-21.md) plus the four findings rated BREAKS. The tester's BlackBerry-style QWERTY phone is ~393x590dp: NORMAL width, two-thirds the usual height. Every threshold in core/ui/breakpoints.dart keys off WIDTH, so it classifies `regular`, takes the full 1.22 type bump and gets chromeScale 1.0 - none of RESP-SMALL-1's relief reaches it. FIXES, all structural rather than dimensional: (1+2) chat_thread/composer.dart _openWriteHelp and _showReplyIdeas were showModalBottomSheet WITHOUT isScrollControlled, which caps a sheet at 9/16 of screen height, over non-scrolling Column(min) bodies of ~468dp and ~372dp - at 590dp tall the cap is 332dp so the last two write-help rows (including 'Reply ideas') and the last reply suggestion were laid out past the bottom of the sheet with no way to scroll to them; both now set isScrollControlled and wrap their rows in Flexible+SingleChildScrollView, the idiom _pickTransLang already used. (3) call_screen.dart's audio layout was a Positioned.fill SingleChildScrollView over the header row: Scrollable hit-tests OPAQUE, so the back/minimize buttons were painted but dead, and on a 590dp screen the 350dp hero centred 24dp from the top and painted through the peer's name; it is now Positioned(top: _headerReserve) so the header sits outside the viewport. (4) that same minHeight expression goes NEGATIVE (invalid BoxConstraints) on a connected call with the keyboard up on a short screen - 590 - 300 - 366 = -76 - and is now clamped at 0. Findings rated CLIPS/TIGHT (width-derived hero height, ZineAppBar's fixed 76dp band, RichPickerPanel's 300dp default, AskAva empty state) are documented with a proposed heightClass/isShort/heroHeightFraction API for breakpoints.dart, NOT implemented - that file has another owner. Client-only: no worker change, no schema change, no new flag, no new event.

Nothing here emits, gates or branches on anything: two sheets gain isScrollControlled + a scrollable body, one Positioned.fill becomes Positioned(top:), one BoxConstraints value is clamped. There is no property whose value could be read back to prove it, and inventing an event to satisfy the gate would be worse than saying so. CONCRETE VISUAL CHECK instead, on a short device (or the 393x590 / 320x480 emulator profiles): (a) in a chat thread open Help me write better - all FIVE rows must be present and 'Reply ideas' tappable; (b) run Reply ideas with a wordy incoming message - all three suggestions reachable, scrolling if needed; (c) place an audio call and confirm the peer's NAME is legible above the hero art and that the header back arrow actually minimizes the call (it did not before); (d) answer a call and open the text-note composer with the keyboard up - no red overflow, no constraints assertion.

CALL-ACCEPT-STATUS-KILL-1.description: Caller-side accept-kills-call race (the 2026-08-08 18:10 IST davy↔Tiger ghost-calling cascade, prod call avatok-b3e2da5c). callCommand's FCM durable backstop pushed EVERY changed command's wire status to the peer, including `accept`; on the caller, CallSession._statusSub's catch-all ended any not-yet-connected session with whatever status arrived, so when the accept push beat WebRTC connect the caller killed the call at the moment of accept, auto-cancelled, and the callee's freshly-accepted call died — followed by instant redial → busy → retry storm. Fix is two-layered: worker only fans out terminal/handoff statuses (protects shipped clients on deploy); client catch-all ignores non-terminal statuses and emits call_status_ignored_nonterminal (next build).

success.note: PRESENCE IS THE BUG SIGNAL: the target is ZERO call_ended reason=accept events after the worker deploy. Any occurrence means a caller session was still torn down by an accept status — either the worker filter regressed or an old worker is live.

Client guard (next build). Zero expected once the worker filter is live; any occurrence is the guard correctly swallowing a stray non-terminal status (replay/old worker) instead of killing the call — benign, but worth a look if it spikes.

Ava now opens a forwarded PSTN call with a bare "Hello?", learns who is calling and what they want in a few sentences, refuses to engage with the subject matter (no product talk, no domain answers, no offers to connect), and ends the call herself. The one-line "<who> called about <what>" summary + an intent category ride on the end_call tool's NEW `summary`/`category` arguments — same Gemini session, no second model (owner decision 2026-06-30) — and become the inbox card headline (summary.reason, which the frozen client renderer already displays) and the push body. A 6-min DO ALARM watchdog force-finalizes a stuck session, and the settle is capped at hard_cap_ms so a stuck session can never bill past the cap.

success.note: message_taken equivalent: this lane's canonical outcome event carrying the one-liner. The slack covers the REAL cases where Ava never reaches end_call and so cannot emit a summary — the caller hangs up first, the hard cap fires, or the watchdog fires. Those calls still deliver a recording; they just have no headline. A pass rate near 0 means the end_call summary/category arguments are not being produced at all.
Two DISTINCT persons on the new build (two-sided: caller + callee). balance_exhausted here would mean the zero-stop, not the PA, ended the screening.

billed/call ms coherence. billed_ms is the settle's own duration and is capped at receptHardCapMs (5 min once the timer flip lands). billed_ms > call_ms, or billed_ms above the cap, is the billing bug this pair of props exists to make queryable.

PRESENCE IS THE BUG SIGNAL (spec 6a): the target is ZERO of these in the soak window. min_events 0 so an empty result is the pass; if any DO fire, settle_trued_up=true means the session ran past the cap and the settle was capped — investigate the hung leg.
The delivery half, decoupled from the call half. false here = the recording and message never reached the callee's inbox even though the call summary said the call completed.

NOTIF-REACT-1.description: Phase 3 of Specs/NOTIF-PARITY-PLAN.md — the owner's third screenshot, "X reacted <emoji> to your message". Two things were quietly untrue before this. (1) The CLIENT NEVER CALLED POST /api/msg/react at all: kMsgReactUrl was declared in core/config.dart and grep found it referenced in exactly one file, its own declaration. Reactions rode the PartyKit relay only, so they were never persisted and vanished on reinstall. (2) Because the server never heard about a reaction, there was nothing to notify from — the feature was unbuildable, not merely unbuilt. message_actions.dart _react now POSTs the reaction with a target_uid naming the AUTHOR of the reacted-to message; reactMsg validates that uid is a member of the conversation and is not the reactor, then enqueues kind:'reaction'; consumers/src/fcm.ts renders it data-only; the client folds it into that conversation's EXISTING MessagingStyle card as one more line rather than a competing notification, and does not bump the launcher badge because a reaction is not an unread message. An unresolvable author means NO push rather than a guess — guessing 'in a DM it must be the other person' is wrong the moment someone reacts to their own message.

success.note: SERVER side. chat_reaction already fired before this change and will keep firing whether or not anyone is notified, so its arrival proves nothing — ship-gate rule 3. notified=true means an author was resolved, validated as a member, was not the reactor, and the push was actually enqueued. When false, notify_reason distinguishes an old client that sent no target_uid from a queue rejection, which a bare false cannot.

CLIENT side, on the AUTHOR's device — the other half. The server can enqueue happily while the recipient's app drops it. Needs two people on the newest build: one to write a message, the other to react to it.

NOTIF-SYNC-1.description: Phase 4 (part) of Specs/NOTIF-PARITY-PLAN.md: reading a conversation on one device takes its notification down on the user's OTHER devices. readMsg now enqueues a silent data-only kind:'notif_clear' addressed to ctx.uid — the reader's own devices, never a peer — mirroring the existing del/hide silent lane; the client clears that conversation's shade log, cancels its notification and re-counts the bundle summary. This mattered little before NOTIF-STYLE-1, when a single shared banner was simply overwritten by the next message; now that every chat owns a persistent card, a chat read elsewhere would otherwise sit in the other device's shade indefinitely and keep inflating the 'N messages from M chats' line.

success.note: had_conv=true means the silent push arrived AND carried a conversation to clear. The event firing with had_conv=false would mean the payload lost the conv id in transit, which clears nothing while looking like a success. Genuinely needs the same account signed in on two devices to observe; min_devices_on_build is 1 because it is not two-SIDED (no second person is involved), but it is untestable on a single handset.

CALL-PREROLL-1.description: Specs/PLAN-CALL-INSTANT-PICKUP-2026-08-16.md, extending CALL-PREWARM-1/2 — the callee pre-rolls its WHOLE media path during the ring, not just the ICE+seat join: CallPrewarm._preroll acquires the mic (track disabled), builds an isolated peer connection with no session handlers, PUBLISHES (silent) and PULLS the caller's audio (muted, via a passive onTrack cache mirroring CallSession._prejoinEarlyTracks). CallSession._bootMedia peeks the pre-rolled stream (non-consuming) before getUserMedia, audio-only calls only. _startSfuMedia's hasFullPreroll branch (gated on the returned stream being IDENTICAL to the one CallPrewarm.adopt was called with) promotes the connection via the new _promotePrerollPc — installs onTrack/onConnectionState for the first time, unmutes the local track (done earlier, at peek) and each cached remote track, then replays them through the extracted _handleRemoteTrack ladder instead of re-running publish/pull. Gated on callPrerollV1 stacked on top of callPrewarmOnRingV1; either off is byte-identical to CALL-PREWARM-2's already-shipped behaviour.

success.note: The ring-time preroll actually finished BOTH legs before accept. Companion assertion on the SAME event: pulled must also be true (checked separately below) — published alone means the callee could publish but the caller's own ring-time audio was never found.

The peer's audio was pulled and muted BEFORE accept, during the ring — the whole point of this issue. Both this and the published assertion must be observed from the SAME call_preroll_ready event to mean anything; two different calls each satisfying one half is not evidence the fast path ever ran end to end.

The callee's own headline number. Must sit under ~2000ms on wifi once call_preroll_ready(published, pulled) has fired for the same call — CALL-PREWARM-1's baseline was ~1.5-2s; this issue's whole purpose is cutting the remaining publish+pull cost on top of that. `equals: ""` is a presence-only placeholder for a numeric field the manifest checker cannot range-check; read the actual value.

Also confirm a DECLINED or missed call leaves no mic indicator lit afterward (CallPrewarm.discard/_closeEntry teardown).

DELETE-UNHIDE-1.description: Owner report 2026-08-17: 'old deleted messages come back when I load the app'. sync_hub's hidden-flag seed recorded BOTH values from the server `hidden` column, and HiddenStore.mergeBulk overwrites unconditionally (unlike its monotonic sibling ReadStateStore.mergeBulk beside it). So every sync copied hidden=0 back over a locally hidden message and un-deleted it — permanently, because the local flag was then false too and nothing re-posts it. The hide POST is fire-and-forget with no retry and no outbox and is skipped entirely when evId is null, so hides made offline or that failed never reached the server at all. The seed now writes only `true`; un-hiding still works through the explicit Undo and the `hide` push.
DELETE-UNHIDE-1.no_telemetry: This removes a write; there is no new event and the correct outcome is the ABSENCE of resurrected messages, which no event can assert. Verified by reading the two stores' merge semantics side by side (chat_state.dart ReadStateStore.mergeBulk is monotonic, HiddenStore.mergeBulk was not) rather than by telemetry. Field check: a message deleted for me, app force-closed and reopened, stays deleted.

DELETE-CHAT-1.description: 'Delete chat' in the thread overflow menu was literally `() => Navigator.pop(context)` — it closed the sheet and did nothing: no local wipe, no server call, no confirmation. The server's thread-clear machinery (threadClear, the thread_clears table, its /sync snapshot) has been complete for a while and the client had NO half of it — no store, no sender, no reader. So a 'deleted' chat was never deleted and /api/msg/sync re-materialised the backlog on the next launch. Adds ThreadClearStore (a per-conversation cleared-through cursor in epoch seconds, monotonic), a confirm dialog, an on-screen wipe, ChatPreviewStore.remove so the chat-list subtitle goes too, and render-time filters on the cache-restore and cold-open paths. A CURSOR rather than a row wipe because sync re-inserts rows unconditionally, so a wipe would only hold until the next connection. LOCAL ONLY for now: the server keys its cursor on a canonical message id that is not reachable from this screen, so cross-device clear is deliberately not faked.

success.note: The event firing at all is meaningful here ONLY because the button previously had no code path that could emit anything — but the property is what proves the handler ran to completion. Two blockers were caught in review before this shipped and both would have made the fix a silent no-op: the cursor was loaded in initState where _convKey is still null, and an extra Navigator.pop closed the thread route so `mounted` was false by the time the user confirmed, skipping the wipe AND this event. scope='local_only' is also the honest marker that this clear does not yet reach the user's other devices.

MEDIA-CARD-SAFE-1.description: Song/video job-card safety pass after the 2026-08-17 owner report ("unable to share the song and the app crashes" + "AI media job timeouts"). Three changes, all client-side, no worker change, no new flag. (1) Share no longer aborts when the pre-share refresh round-trip fails: _shareJobArtifact falls back to the last-known job record and to a share link this session already minted (AiMediaJobRepository._shareLinks), and says "Can't share this song while you're offline" instead of "try again in a moment" when there is genuinely nothing to hand the share sheet. (2) AiMediaJobRepository.fetch coalesces concurrent callers per job_id, holds a 15s cooldown after an offline failure, and reports connectivity failures as ai_media_job_fetch_offline instead of a $exception; _AvaImageBubbleImage now re-mints at most once per mount, which is what produced 30+ concurrent 10s timeouts in a single second. (3) Null-safety/memory: the two Image.memory(thumbnailBytes!) force-unwraps in ai_media_job_card.dart are gone, and _fetchArtifactBytes stops making a second full copy of every downloaded artifact.

success.note: Emitted synchronously on the Share tap, BEFORE any network call, so a share that dies mid-flight is visible as a share_started with no matching ai_media_job_artifact_share. Absence on the new build means the Share control never reaches _shareJobArtifact at all. Carries has_cover and cover_status so a coverless song can be told apart from a normal one without guessing.

THE value assertion. ok=true is the only thing that means a song actually reached the OS share sheet. ok=false with error=no_link_no_artifact is the new honest offline path and must NOT be read as a pass.

DELETE-CHAT-XDEV-1.description: Makes 'Delete chat' reach every device of the user's, completing DELETE-CHAT-1. The server half has existed since [MSG-DELETE-1] and NOTHING called it: threadClear keeps a monotonic per-conv cursor in the actor's own InboxDO, wakes their other devices, and snapshots thread_clears into every /sync — but `grep thread_clear app/lib` returned zero hits, and consumers/src/fcm.ts had no branch for kind:'thread_clear' either, so even the wake push produced no payload. Adds: the FCM branch; a client POST with a synthesised cursor_mid; the missing /sync reader; and a foreground push branch that syncs immediately. The cursor is synthesised as '<nowMs padded to 13>.ffffffff' — NOT a fake message id: canonicalMsgId is zero-padded precisely so ids sort as strings, and the server only ever MAX-compares this value, never dereferences it, so an upper bound for the current millisecond is the correct thing to send. Self-scoped: touches only the actor's own InboxDO, zero peer writes and zero peer pushes.

success.note: Server-side, and it asserts the SAFETY invariant rather than mere arrival: peer_writes=0 proves a self-clear never touched the other person's inbox. The event has existed since [MSG-DELETE-1] and has NEVER fired, because no client called the route — so its first appearance is also the proof the client half now exists. Pair with chat_thread_clear_sent (ok=true) on the device.

CALL-STAGE0A-1.description: Stage 0A (server-only): ExecutionContext threaded into all 7 callSfu* handlers + guard(); the 12 awaited trackUser sends moved to ctx.waitUntil via an sfuTrack() wrapper, removing a queue round trip from the response path of join/publish/pull (latency introduced 2026-08-16 by TELEMETRY-AWAIT-1). The telemetry-only emailFor lookup moved OUT of guard() and INTO the deferred work, so no identity read (KV, or Clerk on a cold miss) sits in front of a media operation; emailFor also gains a bounded in-isolate memo (60s TTL, 500 entries). Deterministic PER-CALL sampling (FNV-1a over call_id) at rate 1.0 today, errors never sampled.

success.note: Server-side elapsed_ms on call_sfu_joined/published/pulled must DROP versus the 2026-08-17 baseline (join 365-1041ms, publish 630-2318ms, pull 646-1284ms) while sfu_ms stays flat - that delta is exactly the telemetry+identity work removed from the response path. At rate 1.0 no event may go missing.

CALL-VIDEO-FIX-1.description: Audio->video switch froze the call. Three confirmed causes fixed together (they must ship together; the mid alone is not sufficient): (a) publishVideo sent a HARD-CODED mid '1' which, after remote audio had been pulled, often belonged to the remote audio transceiver - now the real mid is resolved from pc.getTransceivers() by matching sender.track.id, and the upgrade ABORTS rather than guessing if unresolvable; (b) publishVideo ended with unawaited(_pull('video')) launching a second concurrent negotiation - now awaited; (c) nothing serialized negotiations - CallSfuTransport now has a negotiation queue (_serialize) with a 15s per-op timeout covering connectPublish/connectPull/publishVideo/_pull/pullPeerVideo/pullPeerAudio, plus a generation gate (_ownsNegotiation) so a timed-out body cannot clobber _pc/_sessionId of its successor. The initial connect publish keeps mids '0'/'1' deliberately: tracks are added audio-then-video before the first offer with nothing else on the PC, so they are correct by construction.

success.note: Switching a live audio call to video must: not freeze, keep AUDIO uninterrupted, emit local_video_published then remote_video_track_attached then remote_video_first_frame on the peer, and emit NO call_video_upgrade_failed. call_sfu_negotiation shows queued_ms/ran_ms with no overlapping ops.

CALL-VIDEO-FIX-3.description: CallRoom /sfu-seat carried audio/video track names and mids forward from the PREVIOUS seat even when the session_id changed. A reconnect or prewarm/adopt swap therefore published a new session paired with dead track names, and the peer pulled a track that no longer existed - silent one-way audio. Carry-forward is now scoped to the same session id; a session change starts clean.

success.note: After an SFU reconnect (call_sfu_reconnected), the following pull must succeed against the NEW session; no peer_track_not_published 409 storm and no one-way audio.

CALL-PREJOIN-2.description: Caller pre-publish now starts on a POSITIVE RING-ACK instead of the socket 'welcome' frame. A ring-ack is the server confirming it enqueued the ring, which it can only do for a call it has already recorded with caller_uid and callee_uid set - exactly the precondition POST /sfu-seat checks. Firing from 'welcome' raced call placement and returned 403 not_a_participant (prod avatok-af94b158). Publishing during the ring means the callee's first pull finds a live track instead of both phones waiting on each other after Accept - the 'connected, meter running, hello? hello?' silence.

success.note: Caller emits call_prejoin_published DURING the ring with no call_sfu_error stage=seat_register. On the same call the callee's stage_sfu_pull_audio minus stage_sfu_publish must shrink (mutual wait gone), and the CALLER's call_connected must still be AFTER the callee's accept (the CALL-PREJOIN-ISOLATE-1 regression must not return).

CALL-AUDIBLE-1.description: The UI declared 'connected' 12-16s before inbound audio arrived (owner: 'it says connected, the meter runs, and I keep saying hello'). _connected is load-bearing (ringback stop, talk time, four timer cancels, watchdog+sampler start, receptionist abort, glare clear, onConnectionState gate) so it is deliberately UNCHANGED; a new presentational milestone audibleReady is added instead, driven by the EXISTING first-audio-bytes probe (never audioLevel - a silent caller must still connect). While connected but not audible the UI shows 'Connecting audio...' and hides the call timer, on both the call screen and the minimized pill; the connection haptic moved to this milestone. No-stats paths (RealtimeKit) use trackAdded evidence plus a 4s safety timer so no call can be stuck forever. Flag callAudibleStateV1, default false.

success.note: call_audible_ready must fire on every answered call with ms_from_connected recorded - that number IS the lie we are measuring (12-16s today). call_audible_timeout must be rare and only on no-stats paths. A silent caller must still reach audible.

CALL-NATIVE-ANSWER-1.description: The AvaTOK answer screen took 5.61s to appear after the ring arrived (prod avatok-1204d417: call_incoming_shown 15:06:58.241 -> call_branded_fsi_routed 15:07:03.847), because _routeToBrandedIncoming polls navigatorKey.currentState every 250ms while the Flutter engine cold-starts. MainActivity now paints an INTERACTIVE native ring screen (caller name, Decline/Accept, 72dp targets) synchronously on the avatok.incoming_call_tap launch, before Flutter exists, and swaps to the existing passive Connecting overlay on accept. All real accept/decline logic still ends in the EXISTING Dart paths (PushService.acceptRingingCall / declineIncomingCall) via the same pending/drain idiom as pendingIncomingTap; the native screen is a surface only. Native reads the flag from a disk mirror (filesDir/callnative/answer_flags.json) written by RemoteConfig.refresh, fail-closed to OFF. _brandedRouteGate is marked on native action so the independent FCM/WS ring lane cannot stack a duplicate branded screen.

success.note: call_native_ring_shown must fire with ms_from_intent well under 1000ms (target ~100ms) on an incoming call answered from the notification, versus the 5610ms call_incoming_shown->call_branded_fsi_routed baseline. Accepting from the native screen must produce call_native_answer_accept AND the normal call_started/call_connected ladder with NO duplicate IncomingBusinessCallScreen. Declining must end the ring on both phones.

CALL-SILENT-PREWARM-1.description: Default-off 1:1 incoming-call transport prewarm. PREWARMING is entered only after an Inbox liveness probe proves a main Flutter isolate is available. That isolate joins one Cloudflare SFU session and negotiates a datachannel-only RTCPeerConnection with no microphone, media track, publish, pull, renderer, playout, or audio focus. CallRoom alone promotes to RINGING after verified ICE/DTLS readiness or a bounded fallback, anchors caller ringback and Ava timing there, and sends the real ring over live Inbox plus durable FCM. Accept adds media to and adopts the same PC. Nonce/generation/device/session checks, native durable action state, network invalidation, teardown, and durable ring-delivery retry close stale and multi-device races.

success.note: Two-device qualification only: readiness may be emitted only after the datachannel-only PC reaches connected. Any pre-Accept microphone/media event is a release blocker.
Every silent attempt reaches exactly one server-owned real-ring anchor. A rising fallback rate is an optimisation regression; a missing ring-start event is a correctness failure.
Prepared-path two-phone target: actual remote playout within 1.5 seconds of the callee CallSession start. Transport connected alone is not success.

CALL-PREWARM-TRUTH-1.description: The silent transport prewarm claimed a published SFU audio sender that did not exist. hasPrepublishedAudio() tested only `transportFuture != null`, which is true from the moment the attempt starts and stays true after it completes by FAILING. Production runs callSilentTransportPrewarmV1=true with callSfuV1=false, so every incoming ring got call_sfu_blocked reason=flag_off and CallSfuException(sfu_unavailable,503), yet Accept still installed the null-track protocol-silence stream, deferred getUserMedia past the answer (~2.2s measured on 2026-08-20), and the answering phone transmitted silence for the whole call (mic_audio_level=0.0, mic_energy_delta=0) while the peer's jitter buffer happily played it back. Fix: the SFU seat/publish half of the prewarm is skipped entirely when callSfuV1 is off (the ICE warm-up still runs, so P2P pickup stays fast); _prepareTransport marks every exit settled and records join-unavailable as a failure instead of returning silently; hasPrepublishedAudio requires a real sender once settled; call_session gates the protocol-silence branch on callSfuV1 too.

success.note: The answering side must end up with a live enabled mic track. call_preaccept_audio_replaced fired on BOTH broken calls on 2026-08-20, so its ARRIVAL proves nothing; this is the value that does.
While callSfuV1 is false in prod every prewarm must report ice_only. An 'ice_and_sfu_seat' here means the gate did not take and call_sfu_blocked reason=flag_off is back.
Positive proof the new gate ran. Absent, together with call_sfu_blocked reason=flag_off present, means the protocol-silence branch can be entered again.

CALL-ROUTE-AVAIL-1.description: call_audio_owner_conflict fired whenever the confirmed route differed from the intent, without asking whether the intent was reachable at all. A device with no built-in earpiece (every Android emulator, some tablets) can only ever answer 'speaker' to an earpiece request, so it emitted a conflict on every apply of every call - which is exactly what an emulator did on all three test calls on 2026-08-20 and it was read as a device bug. CallAudioController now consults the output-device inventory the Kotlin side already returns in getAudioDiagnostics (output_device_types, an AudioDeviceInfo type CSV; 1 = TYPE_BUILTIN_EARPIECE) and splits the two cases: an unreachable intent emits the new informational call_audio_route_unavailable, while a route that WAS present and still lost stays call_audio_owner_conflict and now carries intent_available and fallback_reason. When the platform reports no inventory (iOS today) the answer is null and the event stays a conflict, so this can never hide a real one. The availability read happens only on the rare apply that missed its intent.

success.note: On a device with no earpiece the earpiece-to-speaker fallback must now land here, not on call_audio_owner_conflict. Verify on the emulator, which is the known-reproducing device.
Anything still called a conflict must have had its route available (true) or unknown (null). An intent_available=false here means the split did not take and the noise is back.

CALL-VOL-AUDIBLE-1.description: Nothing in the app ever looked at the Android STREAM_VOICE_CALL index during a call. push_service already does this check for the RINGER (ring_volume == 0 feeds a 'could not have rung audibly' determination) but the in-call stream had no equivalent, so a call played out at 3/15 was indistinguishable in telemetry from one at 15/15: healthy transport, RTP flowing, jitter buffer emitting 48000 samples/sec, and a user who hears nothing. On 2026-08-20 that ambiguity cost a debugging session. CallSession now emits call_volume_low once per call when voice_volume/voice_volume_max is at or below 0.2, carrying the route, speakerphone state and output_device_types so an emulator at its 3/15 default can be told apart from a real phone whose owner turned the rocker down. Observation only: the app deliberately contains no setStreamVolume or adjustStreamVolume anywhere, because silently overriding someone's call volume can deafen them.

success.note: Set the device call volume low, place a call, and confirm exactly ONE of these per call carrying the real ratio. More than one per call_id means the once-per-call latch broke and the 5s diagnostics cadence is spamming.
Guards against a divide-by-zero device reporting a bogus max and manufacturing a low-volume report on every call.

CALL-PREWARM-TRUTH-2.description: The other half of CALL-PREWARM-TRUTH-1, found by auditing the P2P ordering rather than by another failed call. _startP2pOffer has always acquired the real microphone before _newPC(), but the P2P ANSWER path (case 'offer' in the signalling handler) never did - and the answerer is the only side that can ever have _prewarmAudioPending, because the callee is never the P2P offerer (the decider is). So a callee whose SFU publish aborted to P2P built its peer connection straight from the trackless protocol-silence stream: _addStreamTracks looped zero times without throwing, createAnswer produced a recvonly audio m-line, and the callee shipped silence for the entire call while hearing the caller perfectly. Nothing could repair it afterwards - call_session.dart has no replaceTrack for audio, no onRenegotiationNeeded handler and no audio renegotiation path; the only true renegotiation in the file is video-only and user-triggered. Fix: hoist the same _prewarmAudioPending guard into the offer handler before _newPC(), and make the zero-audio-track case emit call_pc_built_without_audio instead of being a silent no-op. Note CALL-PREWARM-TRUTH-1's callSfuV1 gate already makes this unreachable in production TODAY, since _prewarmAudioPending can no longer be set while callSfuV1 is false; this closes it for the day the SFU is switched on.

success.note: This event should ideally never fire at all. If it fires with prewarm_audio_pending=true the answerer guard did not run and the trackless peer connection is back - that is the original bug, and it is terminal for the call it appears on. Firing with false is a different, unknown defect and still wants investigating.

Two-device qualification. The answering side must reach a live enabled mic track on the P2P path too, not just the SFU replace-track path. Pair with path=fallback to confirm the answer path specifically.

RAJ-INDIGO-1.description: Owner-requested retheme, 2026-08-21. (1) TURQUOISE RETIRED APP-WIDE: AD.headerFooter moved #5CB8A6 -> Jodhpur indigo #2E4A8C, and the last four turquoise values (AD.newGroup, AD.incomingCall, avatar families 'mint'/'aqua') moved to marigold / deep green / terracotta. Turquoise was a LIGHT band and indigo is a DARK one, so every header that hardcoded ink (chat_list, chat_thread + its search bar and guardian shield, groups_tab, contact_profile) was re-routed through AD.onBand. (2) STATUS BAR: chat_list and chat_thread put their band Container OUTSIDE the SafeArea (the arrangement status_screen.dart already used) so the header colour reaches the top of the screen; chat_list's tab bodies got MediaQuery.removePadding(removeTop) because they stopped being descendants of that SafeArea and would otherwise re-apply the inset. (4) TAB CHIPS: Chats/Groups/Calls and Contacts/Dialpad/Block list/Call logs each carry a permanent Rajasthani accent with an ink outline and a hard offset shadow; the AvaDialer strip in particular was cream-on-cream (fill AvaDialTheme.surface2, fg onBand) and unreadable. (5) Contact info header rebuilt to the Profile recipe: rani band to the top of the screen, FlowerChainSeam, profileHero petal ring around the avatar. Client-only: no worker change, no schema change, no new flag.
RAJ-INDIGO-1.no_telemetry: Presentation chrome. No code path is gated, no branch changed, and no event could carry a failure value — the same reasoning as [RAJ-SEAMS-1]. Success is VISUAL and must be read off a device on the newest $app_build, in this order. RESP-SMALL-1.description: Owner report 2026-08-21: a tester on a ~3x4 inch phone cannot see or reach content — 'everything moves away from her screen and she is unable to scroll down.' ROOT CAUSE: main.dart's MaterialApp builder applied a FLAT baseBump of 1.22 at every width, so the app enlarged all type (and every text-driven height) by 22% on the smallest devices. The existing width-aware ceiling did not help because it sat ABOVE the bump — on a <320dp phone with a normal OS font setting the resolved scale was clamp(1.22, 0.85, 1.20) = 1.20, still a 20% enlargement. A ceiling can only cap a large OS font setting; it cannot undo a bump the app applies itself. FIX: baseBump now ramps with width (>=360 stays 1.22 per the standing [APP-TYPE-SCALE-2] owner decision; 320-360 -> 1.10; <320 -> 1.00) and each ceiling was lowered to sit at or just above its own bump. Second lever: a new ZineBreakpoints.chromeScale(context) (1.0 / 0.85 / 0.72) trims UNSCROLLABLE chrome only — SquiggleSeam and DoubleWaveSeam heights and their wave geometry, the AvaTalk header's vertical padding, the tab strip's bottom padding, and the chat-thread header height (floored at 48 so it cannot overflow the 46px IconButton constraints inside it). Type and tap targets are deliberately NOT scaled by it. Third: width_class and resolved_text_scale are now on the event envelope so any future report from a small device is filterable in PostHog. Client-only: no worker change, no schema change, no new flag.

success.note: THE FIX ITSELF, as a number. Before this change an xcompact device resolved to 1.20 with a normal OS font setting; the new ramp caps that class at 1.10. min_events is 0 because the owner's own fleet may contain no xcompact device at all — absence is a pass, a value above 1.10 is a regression. This is the assertion that would have caught the original bug, since screen_metrics was already reporting resolved_text_scale=1.2 for her phone and nobody read it.

THE GUARDRAIL, and the more important of the two. 1.22 on normal phones is an explicit owner decision made AFTER 1.10 was shipped and rejected as too small ([APP-TYPE-SCALE-2]). The obvious wrong fix for a small-screen report is to lower the bump everywhere, which would silently re-break every normal handset including the owner's. If this assertion fails, the small-screen fix leaked into the regular class.

Shrinking fixed-height chrome is exactly the change that causes overflow, and the chat-thread header is the known risk (46px IconButton constraints inside a scaled box, floored at 48 for this reason). width_class is on the envelope as of this change, so an overflow on a small device is now attributable to one instead of being lost in the general exception stream.

LIB-READABLE-1.description: Owner report 2026-08-21 with screenshots: every tile in AvaLibrary > Images rendered as a blank black square with just a JPG/PNG chip, and tapping one said 'Could not open this file'. ROOT CAUSE: both the thumbnail path (lib_thumbs._privateRoute) and the open path (MediaService.downloadLibraryItem) decided 'can I read these bytes?' by SNIFFING THE URL STRING for 'X-Amz-Signature'. The worker returns TWO valid signed-URL shapes for a private file: a real R2 SigV4 presign (has that parameter) and, whenever the R2 S3 keys are not configured, an HMAC fallback at /api/media/private-read?key&exp&sig (does not). A row that took the fallback was misfiled as unreadable E2E ciphertext; with no enc_blob — which the uploader never gets for their own row — the client drew the type tile and threw 'private file has no decryption material' on tap. Replaced with a structural LibraryItem.isDirectlyReadable used by BOTH paths, so the two can no longer be wrong in the same way while looking like separate bugs. Also fixed AvatarCache.transformUrl silently dropping the query string (it rebuilt scheme+host+path only), which stripped the signature off any private URL routed through sizedUrl and produced a 404 — a second, independent way the same tiles came back blank. Also instrumented the viewer's bare catch(_), which had made this failure completely invisible in PostHog. Client-only: no worker change, no schema change, no new flag.

UPDATE-ABI-OFFSET-1.description: Owner report 2026-08-21: after shipping build 10603 his app still said 'You're on the latest version'. Diagnosed from PostHog: his device reports app_version 0.1.18+12601, build 12601, release SHA a51b976a — which is run #601. ROOT CAUSE: the side-load APK step passed `--split-per-abi`, and Flutter's Gradle plugin adds 1000*abiCode to versionCode for split APKs (arm64-v8a = +2000). So the APK was stamped 2000 + 10000 + run_number while the .aab AND the latestAppBuild KV pointer both used 10000 + run_number. Any tester who side-loaded the APK — which is exactly what we told him to do when the Play link was broken — installed a build number 2000 higher than the pointer will ever reach, so UpdateService computed latest(10603) <= current(12601) and reported up-to-date on every future release, permanently. The side-load workaround was itself what disabled his updates. FIX: dropped --split-per-abi (`--target-platform android-arm64` already limits this to one ABI, so the flag bought nothing but the offset), updated the staging step for the new `app-release.apk` filename with a hard error if a per-ABI file reappears, and added an aapt2 assertion that the APK's actual versionCode equals the pointer. CI-only: no app code, no worker change, no schema change, no new flag.

success.note: THE FIX, as a number. Every CI build number is 10000 + run_number, so a healthy installed build is in [10000,10999]. The broken APKs installed as 12xxx. An installed_build >= 11000 on the new build means the ABI offset is back and that device's update check is permanently dead. NOTE: devices already on 12601 will keep reporting 12xxx until they uninstall and reinstall — this assertion is about NEW installs of the fixed APK, so read it against first-seen devices.

Secondary. A device sitting on an older build must not be told it is current. Combined with the assertion above this catches the pointer/APK mismatch from either direction — a stale pointer or an inflated installed build both surface here as a wrong up_to_date.

CALL-VOICE-2026.description: Recipient voice-note playback. A recorded voice note uploads PLAINTEXT to the private `digital` R2 bucket (MediaService.uploadPlaintext, owner decision 2026-07-25) and the SENDER caches its own bytes at upload time, so the sender's bubble plays forever. The recipient's only way in is `digitalUrl` — a 900-SECOND presigned read minted for the sender and copied into the envelope — which chat_thread/persistence.dart persists verbatim and restores verbatim, so ~15 minutes after delivery it is a dead credential. The documented recovery (MediaService._resolveStaleDigitalUrl) needs the RECIPIENT's own AvaLibrary row, and that row is created only when a server conv id happened to be resolvable at arrival AND the worker's two-sided membership check passed (routes/media.ts libraryRecord rejects a `digital` row 400 conv_required / 403 forbidden otherwise) — and the whole call is fire-and-forget behind a swallowing catch. Miss either and the note is unplayable on the recipient's phone forever. FIX: MediaService.prefetchReceived() pulls the bytes into the SAME per-account cache (media/<AccountScope.id>/<hash>) the instant the envelope arrives, while the credential is still alive, turning a 900s window into the permanent local-first cache every other attachment already has — no privacy boundary moves, no bytes become server-readable that were not already, blossom/E2E media is not touched. ALSO: (a) _playAudio's tap guard swallowed EVERY tap while any note was loading with zero user feedback — a 0ms window on the sender (localBytes in memory) but up to 30s on the recipient, which is literally 'tapping play does nothing'; now silent only for a repeat tap on the same note. (b) _audioTrackId's pre-upload fallback keyed on `_seq`, a counter that restarts on every cold open, so a track was renamed on restart and its saved position orphaned; now keyed on the durable rumor id. (c) Every one of the six pipeline stages now emits a stage-tagged failure instead of one untyped event. Client-only: no worker change, no schema change, no new flag.

success.note: THE assertion. `mine=false` is the entire point: a voice_note_played from the SENDER has always worked and proves nothing — that is exactly how this bug survived. This is a note the tapping user DID NOT SEND, playing, with non-empty bytes. Zero rows on the newest $app_build means the recipient side is still dead however many sender-side plays landed.

The failure-VALUE half (2026-08-08 lesson). A recipient-side failure at resolve_download means the presigned URL expired and no library row existed to re-mint from — i.e. the prefetch did not run or did not land. empty_bytes/media_missing mean the envelope reached the recipient without usable ChatMedia. Any of the three on the new build means the fix did not take, even while voice_note_played rows exist from other notes.

The fix's own mechanism, asserted directly: the recipient pulled a digital voice note into the on-device cache while the envelope's credential was still fresh. ok=false here (or no rows at all) means the eager fetch never succeeded and playback is back to racing a 900-second expiry.

STREAM-RECEPTIONIST-1.description: Closes the gap reported 2026-08-24: on the Stream lane (streamCallsEnabled=true in prod, so ALL 1:1 calls) an unanswered call rang forever and never reached Ava, and a dead phone rang forever too. The four-ring handoff lives entirely in the legacy CallRoom DO, which counts the CALLEE's device-ringing receipts and fires handoff_to_receptionist at receptionistRings — and the Stream lane never creates a CallRoom, so nothing counted and nothing fired. This was the TODO(STREAM-RECEPTIONIST-1) at stream_video_calls.ts:996. Two halves. SERVER: streamCallPlace now reads callee presence (readPresenceRead, gated on callPresenceRouting, same presenceFreshSec/presenceOfflineSec thresholds and the same fail-open-on-read-error rule as the legacy offline branch in api.ts) and, when the callee is provably not checking in AND receptionistNoAnswerEligibility(env, callee, 'unreachable') passes, refuses with code 'receptionist' + routing_reason 'offline' + a start payload carrying activation_mode 'unreachable' — no Stream call is created, so an off phone costs nothing. receptionistNoAnswerEligibility gained an activationMode parameter (default 'rings', so every existing caller is unchanged) because the offline path was previously gated by the owner's not-picked-up toggle instead of their unreachable one. CLIENT: the caller's own phone owns the ring window (receptionistRings x ringCycleMs, clamped 20-120s, outgoing only) since this lane has no server ring accounting; on expiry it cancels the Stream ring, ends the call server-side and pushReplacements to the new StreamAvaScreen, which drives a ReceptionistCall — lane-agnostic, because receptionistStart's call_id is optional and every CALL_ROOMS interaction inside it is guarded by if(callId). New client flag getter RemoteConfig.receptionistRings (already in PlatformConfig, DEFAULTS=4 and numericKeys, so not a fake flag).

Zero of these on the new build means the ring window never elapsed into Ava and the presence refusal never routed — i.e. the reported bug is still live. No such event existed before this change, so absence is unambiguous. activation_mode is asserted as a VALUE so this is not an 'events are flowing' check: a 'rings' handoff proves the client ring window fired, an 'unreachable' one proves the server presence fast-path fired, and the two are independent halves that must each be seen at least once.

Ava actually PICKED UP — the thing the owner reported never happening. stream_lane_call_ava_handoff only proves the client decided to hand off; this proves the receptionist session reached a live WebSocket. A build carrying handoffs with zero connects means the bridge routes into a dead end, which is worse than the original bug because the caller loses the ring too. Read alongside stream_lane_ava_failed.reason, which names why when it does not connect (insufficient_tokens / scenario_disabled / disabled / network).

The Stream lane is now READING presence rather than ringing blind. `ring_unknown` is what a failed or absent Upstash read produces, and per CLAUDE.md a fleet-wide `presence=unknown decision=ring_unknown` is exactly the pattern that made [CALL-PRESENCE-1] untestable while the report claimed telemetry was flowing. A healthy build should show ring_fresh / ring_stale / receptionist_offline_immediate. 0.8 tolerates a genuine share of Redis timeouts, which fail open by design and must not read as a regression.

STREAM-AVA-AUDIO-1.description: Reported 2026-08-24, immediately after STREAM-RECEPTIONIST-1 shipped: "Ava finally picked up, but her voice was very low, even when I had the speakers on." She was on the EARPIECE and the Speaker button could not move her off it. Three causes, all fixed. (1) CallAudioController is the single owner of the live route ([CALL-AUDIO-OWNER-1]) and its `intent` defaults to CallAudioRoute.earpiece; only call_session.dart (the LEGACY lane) ever calls seed(), so on the Stream lane the intent was never set. ReceptionistCall.start() then calls reassert('recept_prewarm_before'/'_after') around the native engine's startEngine, and _applyInternal applies `intent` whether or not a call was seeded — so both reasserts actively pulled Ava to the earpiece and pinned her there. StreamAvaScreen now seeds the controller with CallAudioRoute.speaker BEFORE start() and applies it, so those two reasserts hold the speaker instead of undoing it, installs onRouteConfirmed to keep Ava's speaker flag and the button in sync, and releases ownership on dispose. (2) The Speaker button called ReceptionistCall.setSpeaker directly, which only writes the native engine and never the owner — while callAudioOwnerV1 is on that is a race the owner wins, which is why the button looked dead. It now does setIntent then apply (the documented order) and only then tells the engine. (3) _handOffToAva called cancelRinging, which rejects at Stream's coordinator but never calls leave(); this device had already join()ed, so the WebRTC session kept holding the mic and the communication-mode route while Ava played through it. It now leaves the Stream call before opening Ava. Also two affordance fixes: the speaker button highlighted when the speaker was OFF (both here and on stream_call_screen.dart) and Ava now starts on speaker. Client-only; no worker change, no schema change, no new flag.

success.note: The CONFIRMED native route once Ava's session is up — not the requested intent, which is what made this invisible before. `confirmed` comes from CallAudioController.confirmedRouteName, i.e. what NativeVoiceAudio.selectRoute actually landed on, so `speaker` here is the direct refutation of the reported symptom. Asserting the requested intent instead would have passed all along while Ava stayed on the earpiece. 0.9 allows a device genuinely routed elsewhere by the OS (wired headset or bluetooth connected, where speaker is the wrong answer and the fallback is correct).

The Speaker button now reaches the route owner at all. `applied` is false when CallAudioController.apply returned null, which is exactly the silent path the old direct-to-engine call took. This is a failure-path-adjacent assertion: it only appears on a build where someone actually tapped Speaker, so read it against stream_lane_ava_connected on the same build rather than against total call volume.

ReceptionistCall's OWN view of the route it started with (receptionist_call.dart emits this from startEngine's result). Cross-checks the seed from the other side of the boundary: if this is false while stream_lane_ava_audio_route says speaker, the screen and the engine disagree and the reasserts are fighting again. Note this event is shared with the legacy lane, so filter to the new build.

STREAM-AVA-COPY-1.description: Four reports against the new Ava screen on 2026-08-24. (1) The caller's own avatar was a bare '?' — both push sites omit myName/myAvatarUrl and nothing in the Stream lane carries the signed-in user's profile, so Avatar fell through to its placeholder; the screen now reads ProfileStore().load() itself. (2) The status copy contradicted itself: 'Ava is picking up...' followed, at the moment she DID pick up, by "They can't be reached", which read as failure. It now says "Sonal didn't pick up, so you're talking to her assistant" (rings) or "Sonal can't be reached right now, so you're talking to her assistant" (unreachable), with a wrap-up line naming who will get the message. (3) The pronoun is the callee's own. users.gender already existed (migrations/add_user_gender.sql, used by lib/pa_prompt.ts) but was never exposed to the other party; publicIdentityFor now selects and normalises it into its existing 300s KV snapshot, receptionistConfigFor returns owner_first_name/owner_display_name/owner_gender, and a new per-account on-device cache (core/peer_identity_cache.dart, scopedKey/readScoped per the rulebook) makes the first frame correct with no network. Unknown gender renders they/their and is NEVER inferred from the name. (4) The header and Ava's label now use the resolved display name rather than the raw routed value. No schema change (the column predates this), no new flag.

success.note: The callee's pronoun actually REACHED the caller's device. This is the assertion that would have caught the whole class of bug: the field existed in D1 and was used server-side for a year, and the caller's UI still could not say 'her'. `has_gender` false on a build where the callee HAS set a gender means publicIdentityFor, receptionistConfigFor or the client parse dropped it. 0.8 tolerates genuinely unset profiles, which are a real and permanent share of users and correctly render they/their.

The sentence can name the person instead of saying 'They'. Separate from has_gender on purpose: a user can have a name and no stated gender, and the copy has a distinct fallback for each, so one assertion could not prove the other.
