STREAM-AVA-UI-1.description: Presentation fixes on the Ava screen, reported 2026-08-24 from one screenshot: the two avatars were tiny (84px / r42) on a screen with nothing else on it, Ava's avatar was greyed to 45% opacity for the whole connecting phase (which reads as disabled, not connecting), and the animation showing both sides communicating was missing. Avatars are now 132px; the dim is gone; and _LinkFlow replaces it — dots travelling along a rail between the two faces, moving TOWARD whoever is currently speaking and coloured indigo for Ava / marigold for the caller, driven by the same ReceptionistCall.micLevel and avaLevel notifiers the per-face halo uses, with a slow drift toward Ava while connecting so waiting looks alive. One 2s ticker, six dots, one CustomPainter, no import of the legacy lane's _LinkPainter (the two lanes must stay independent). Labels ellipsize under a fixed width so "Sonal's Ava" cannot shift the layout. Client-only; presentation only.
STREAM-AVA-UI-1.no_telemetry: Presentation only: no code path, no gate, no new event, and no property that could carry a failure value. The animation is driven entirely by micLevel/avaLevel, whose real behaviour is already asserted by STREAM-AVA-AUDIO-1 (a confirmed speaker route and a live session) and STREAM-RECEPTIONIST-1 (stream_lane_ava_connected) — if those pass, the notifiers are moving and the link is animating. Visual acceptance is by eye on the screenshot that reported it; inventing an event that fires whenever a widget paints would be an 'events are flowing' check, which the ship gate exists to forbid.

PIVOT-BRAIN-OFF-1.description: Marketplace-first pivot (2026-08-27): the owner asked for AvaBrain ingestion to go dark platform-wide and there was no way to do it. brainEnabled was declared in routes/config.ts DEFAULTS but had ZERO consumers - lib/brain_ingest.ts read no platform config at all and gated only on per-user consent, so the documented brake could not be pulled. It is now read at the top of brainIngest(), before the domain registry lookup, and fails CLOSED on a config read error. Because brainIngest is the single server-lane entry point, this covers do/call_room.ts, lib/recept_stats.ts, routes/brain_media.ts and every future producer without touching them. Drops emit metric brain_ingest_rejected_platform_off and event ingest_rejected_platform_off (tagged with email when the producer passed one).

success.why: Proves real producers are reaching the new gate. Before this change lib/brain_ingest.ts read no platform config at all, so brainEnabled had zero consumers and the platform-wide brake could not be pulled. The event ARRIVING is not enough — flag must carry the key name, or we are looking at some other drop path.
Guards against the new check swallowing the pre-existing device_private hard-reject. device_private must still be reported as its own reason, not collapsed into platform_off.

PIVOT-AI-SWITCHES-1.description: Marketplace-first pivot (2026-08-27): two AI surfaces had no remote kill switch, which blocked both the AI-dark decision and the ShellV2/Marketplace landing. (1) 'Discuss this chat with Ava' was gated only by the compile-time const kDiscussWithAvaEnabled (core/feature_flags.dart:84) - disabling it needed a new APK and a store rollout. (2) AskAva (features/askava/askava_screen.dart) had NO flag whatsoever and was dark only as a side effect of shellV2 being false, so flipping shellV2 true for the Marketplace landing would have shipped an AI surface with no brake. Both keys are now declared in the PlatformConfig interface AND DEFAULTS in worker/src/routes/config.ts (booleans, so no numericKeys entry), with client reads at RemoteConfig.discussWithAvaEnabled / RemoteConfig.askAvaEnabled. AskAva is gated at BOTH the engine (shell_v2.dart _askAva, the single choke point every entry point binds to) and the UI (the AvaBrain slot in app_switcher_bar.dart is hidden, mirroring how the Inbox slot already hides behind pstnVoicemail). Both default TRUE on purpose: declaring the switch must be behaviour-neutral; the dark-ing is a separate deliberate prod flip.

success.why: The whole point of this issue is that AskAva was UNSWITCHABLE. Proving the flip works means seeing the refusal actually fire with the flag name attached - not merely seeing shellv2_askava_opened stop, which would also be the signature of nobody having tapped it.

The inverse assertion. With askAvaEnabled TRUE this must still be PRESENT, proving the gate is a reversible switch and not a one-way kill - the failure mode where a flag ships stuck off and nobody notices because 'the feature is meant to be dark'.

PIVOT-AI-DARK-1.description: Marketplace-first pivot (2026-08-27): aiEnabled was a sledgehammer with no client half. It is declared in routes/config.ts, prod TRUE, and enforced server-side in lib/ai_gate.ts (returns blocked/'ai_disabled'), but NO Flutter file read it - so flipping it off left every AI affordance visibly present in the composer and thread menu, each firing a real request that came back refused. Users would see AI features that are there and broken rather than gone. Added RemoteConfig.aiEnabled (default TRUE, mirroring the server) and wired it into the four in-thread surfaces: the catch-up card, the smart-reply chips, 'Discuss with Ava', and the per-chat 'Ava in this chat' switch. Also suppressed the NETWORK calls, not just the UI - _catchupAvailable, _whatDidIMiss and _maybeFetchSmartReplies now short-circuit before the request, following the generativeEnabled precedent. Separately this gives smartRepliesEnabled its FIRST consumer: it had a RemoteConfig getter and a DEFAULTS entry but zero call sites, so the documented switch did nothing.

success.why: The assertion is a VALUE, not an arrival. With aiEnabled flipped false in prod, real thread-menu opens must report ai_enabled=false - proving devices actually fetched the new config and the client half is live. Measuring the DISAPPEARANCE of AI events instead would be indistinguishable from nobody using chat that day.
Confirms the per-surface flag is being read independently of the master, so the two can be reasoned about separately rather than one masking the other.

PIVOT-MSGR-CALL-OFF-1.description: Marketplace-first pivot (2026-08-27): Messenger 1:1 audio/video calling is killed. New flag messengerCallingEnabled, declared in the PlatformConfig interface AND DEFAULTS in worker/src/routes/config.ts, default FALSE (fail-closed - a config-fetch failure leaves calling off, the correct direction for a feature being removed). Enforced at routeToStreamCallIfEnabled (app/lib/features/avatok/place_1to1_call.dart), the single choke point every human 1:1 dial already passes through, and placed FIRST - before the billing/provider logic, so a refusal can never fall through into a paid path. CRITICALLY it returns TRUE, not false: the function's contract is 'I have taken responsibility, caller must not mount CallScreen', so returning false would route every entry point to the legacy Cloudflare CallScreen which has failed 100% of calls since build 10612 - shipping broken calling instead of no calling. streamCallsEnabled deliberately stays TRUE because the paid consultation/livestream lane shares its SDK, token route and push wiring; the paid lane never calls this function (it routes via features/consult/ and commercial_sessions_api) and is verified untouched. UI hiding of the ~19 affordances and the incoming-push path are separate issues.

success.why: Proves the engine gate is actually reached. The event carries both user_email and peer_email so either side of the attempted call retrieves it - this is a two-sided feature and one device on the build cannot demonstrate it.
Confirms BOTH audio and video are refused. A gate that only caught one of them would look green while half of Messenger calling stayed alive.

Guards the specific mistake this issue exists to avoid: if anyone disables calling by flipping streamCallsEnabled instead, this failure reason reappears and calls fall through to the broken legacy CallScreen. Its ABSENCE is the proof the correct switch was used.

DESIGN-GUARD-ICONS-1.description: tool/check_design_guard.py --check icons was RED at HEAD with 52 bare Material Icons.* across 10 files, against a baseline of 0. The guard only runs on pull_request and this debt landed straight on main, so it never fired. This commit converts only the SIX occurrences in four files that are exclusively this issue's work: the three call_billing screens (billing_hud, consent_sheets, receipt_details) and call_screen.dart, all to PhosphorIcons.<name>(PhosphorIconsStyle.regular). Names were verified against the installed phosphor_flutter 2.1.0 regular set (1512 icons) BEFORE the rewrite rather than guessed - a wrong name is a compile error, and CLAUDE.md records a blind sed producing the non-existent handTokens. The rewrite also breaks const-ness: `const Icon(Icons.x)` becomes `const Icon(PhosphorIcons.x(...))` and a method call cannot appear in a constant expression, so `const` was dropped at the two call_screen sites (const_eval_method_invocation, caught by flutter analyze locally). DELIBERATELY NOT INCLUDED: the remaining 46 occurrences in app/lib/features/virtual_numbers/ (11 files, entirely UNTRACKED) and app/lib/features/avaphone/ava_phone_screen.dart (~724 uncommitted lines). Those belong to another agent's in-flight work in this shared tree; committing them would have published someone else's unfinished feature under this issue id - the exact cross-agent sweeping failure CLAUDE.md documents. The design guard therefore stays RED until that agent lands their work, and the remaining conversions must be done by or with them.
DESIGN-GUARD-ICONS-1.no_telemetry: Presentation-only icon-system migration: no code path, no gate, no flag, no new event, and no property that could carry a failure value. Verification is mechanical and was run: flutter analyze reports 0 errors across the four touched files. Note the guard is NOT yet green overall - 46 violations remain in untracked/in-flight files that this issue deliberately does not touch.

PIVOT-MSGR-CALL-OFF-2.description: UI half of the Messenger-calling kill (engine half is PIVOT-MSGR-CALL-OFF-1). Hides the outgoing call affordances behind RemoteConfig.messengerCallingEnabled so they are NOT BUILT, rather than left visible and failing with a snackbar. Sites: chat_thread.dart header audio+video; contact_detail_screen.dart header Call action and the tap-to-dial gesture on the phone tile (tile kept - it is the only place the number is shown, and long-press-to-copy still works); contact_row_menu.dart 'Call' row; team_inbox.dart 'Call back'; team_ivr_screen.dart warm transfer (no button to hide - the affordance is a dialpad digit press, so the resulting call action is refused with a status message); listing_detail.dart owner-number CTA icon and caption changed from 'tap to message or call' to 'tap to message'. Two sites deliberately NOT gated after investigation: core/calls/call_overlay.dart returnToActiveCall(), which re-mounts an ALREADY-ACTIVE minimised session and is not a dial entry point - gating it would strand a user in a live call, including a paid consultation, and the file already carries the same precedent for streamCallsEnabled; and listing_detail.dart:1441, a QR share-card row whose tap is onCreatorTap (opens the profile), not a call. In chat_thread.dart the flag is nested INSIDE the `else if (!c.group)` branch rather than added to its condition - putting it in the condition would make a 1:1 thread fall through to the next branch and render GROUP-conference buttons driven by group-only state. NOT DONE, blocked: six further sites live in files carrying other agents' uncommitted work (calls_screen.dart, dialpad_search_tab.dart, ava_phone_screen.dart, ava_phone_contacts.dart, shell/v2/avadial_root.dart, askava_screen.dart) and must be gated once that work lands.

success.why: The engine gate (OFF-1) fires when a button was tapped. If the UI hiding works, the hidden entrypoints should STOP appearing in refusals - a refusal still arriving from chat_thread means the button is still on screen and this issue did not land. This asserts the UI change by its effect on the engine's own telemetry rather than by a new event nobody would look at.

PIVOT-MSGR-CALL-OFF-3.description: Incoming half of the Messenger-calling kill. Without it a caller on an OLD build can still ring a phone on the NEW build and it rings normally. Four gates, each refusing before any ringtone, CallKit/notification display or screen push: push_service.dart _showIncoming (after its d['type']!='call' early return), _routeToBrandedIncoming (the dominant production ring lane), and _openCall (placed AFTER the e['group'] early-return so group conferences, governed by conferenceEnabled, are untouched); plus incoming_business_call_screen.dart _accept() and stream_incoming_screen.dart initState()+_onAccept() for a screen already on-screen when the flag flips. THE HARD PART was not refusing paid sessions, which share the same GetStream SDK and push wiring and are the new core product - silently dropping a consultation the customer PAID for is far worse than a Messenger call that still rings. Distinguished by POSITIVE identification, so an unrecognised or future call type still rings: Messenger calls are created with StreamCallType.defaultType() (value 'default', stream_call_service.dart:631,935) while paid sessions are minted server-side as avatok_livestream / avatok_consult_1to1 (worker/src/lib/commercial_stream_sessions.ts) and joined via StreamCallType.fromString (commercial_getstream_handoff.dart:290). Independently verified that the legacy FCM lane cannot carry a paid session at all: _showIncoming returns unless d['type']=='call', and GetStream's native push is early-returned at sender=='stream.video' (push_service.dart:768).

success.why: Two-sided by construction: it takes a caller on an old build and a callee on the new one, so one device cannot demonstrate it - the [CALL-PRESENCE-1] mistake. Proves the callee actually refused rather than simply never being rung.

THE SAFETY ASSERTION, and the one that matters most. Paid consultations and livestreams must STILL RING. This says the Stream ring screen keeps appearing for avatok_consult_1to1 / avatok_livestream while no longer appearing for 'default'. If this event disappears entirely, the gate is eating paid sessions - a money bug - and the fix must be reverted immediately.

PIVOT-NUMBER-MASK-1.description: THE highest-severity item in the marketplace-first pivot. worker/src/routes/number.ts shareCardPut leaked every FREE user's REAL phone number: the comment said 'Paid users share their AvaTOK number; free users their real number', which is the exact opposite of the owner's 2026-08-27 decision that the AvaTOK number is the public identity for EVERYONE. Worse than the comment suggested - the server never computed the number at all, it persisted whatever `number` string the CLIENT posted, so a free-tier client baked the raw real number into the durable share_card blob served to anyone who scanned the QR or resolved the ?t= token. Now the server resolves the number itself from users.avatok_number / avatok_number_display for the authenticated account and IGNORES the client field entirely; with no AvaTOK number assigned it fails CLOSED with 409 no_avatok_number rather than falling back to anything real-number-shaped. JSON shape unchanged - same fields, same snake_case names, only the VALUE of `number` changes and `plan` becomes purely informational. Clients: deep_links.dart no longer branches on sharesRealNumber to decide between Contact.number and Contact.phone; ava_number.dart keeps the sharesRealNumber getter (three other call sites in add_by_link_sheet.dart read it) but hard-returns false, which corrects that file without editing it.

success.why: Share-card writes must CONTINUE after the fix. If they stop, the new fail-closed 409 no_avatok_number path is firing for real users, meaning accounts without an assigned AvaTOK number can no longer share at all - a regression the fix must not cause.

PIVOT-NUMBER-PRIVACY-1.description: Two further real-number exposure paths closed alongside PIVOT-NUMBER-MASK-1. (1) users.private_number stores RAW phone digits with an opt-in show_private_number flag; routes/api.ts resolved an account from that raw real number (SELECT uid FROM users WHERE show_private_number=1 AND private_number=?1), so anyone who knew or guessed a real number could turn it into an AvaTOK identity. number.ts privateNumberSet now hard-writes show_private_number=0 so no NEW row can become exposable - but that does nothing for rows already flagged 1, so the READ in api.ts was deleted outright, which is what actually closes it for existing rows too. Column and field names kept: they are a shipped wire contract, they are simply never read. (2) assign-own let a user bind ANY well-formatted number unverified (phone OTP has been unrouted since 2026-07-10, returning 410) and GET /api/add?n= then resolved it publicly - so someone could claim a real person's number and be findable by it. Chose to keep the binding but exclude it from public resolution rather than disable the endpoint, because exactly one path depends on it end-to-end (ava_number.dart AvaNumber.assignOwn) and disabling would hard-break that flow with no fallback and no data migration. Implemented via a lazily-migrated users.avatok_number_source column (idempotent ALTER guarded like the existing ensureLastSeenCols pattern): assign() stamps 'generated', assignOwn() stamps 'own', and the anonymous ?n=<digits> lookup treats 'own' exactly like not-found (404). The consent-based ?t=<share_token> path is untouched, since that requires the owner to have deliberately shared the link and is not a digit-guessing vector.

success.why: Proves the anonymous digit lookup no longer resolves an unverified self-bound number. A resolve still reporting source='own' means the impersonation vector is open.
The counterweight: normal generated-number resolution must keep working. If this event disappears entirely, the 'own' exclusion is over-matching and has broken add-by-number for everyone.

PIVOT-PAID-NUMBER-1.description: Paid vanity/short AvaTOK numbers bought with TOKENS (1 token = INR 1). Built into avatok_numbers/number.ts, NOT virtual_lines: number.ts does not check virtual_lines, so building there could issue the same number twice the moment virtualNumberFreeEnabled is flipped on. New number flag avatokVanityNumberTokens declared in all THREE required places in config.ts (PlatformConfig interface, DEFAULTS, and numericKeys - a number key missing from numericKeys is un-settable via the API, the same failure class as a fake flag). Default 0 = NOT FOR SALE and the path fails closed with 503 vanity_purchase_disabled; 0 is never treated as free. New purchaseVanity() copies virtualDidPurchase verbatim: stable opId `avatok_vanity:<uid>:<canonical>`, chargeAmount, 402 insufficient_balance, and refund via walletOp credit under a DISTINCT `<opId>:refund` id. It IMPROVES on the template at the charge-succeeded-then-D1-write-failed window: virtualDidPurchase returns ownership_record_failed and leaves the money taken for manual reconciliation, which is only defensible because it has an external provider call to reconcile against; these numbers are pure-virtual and non-PSTN, so there is nothing to reconcile and purchaseVanity refunds immediately instead. Requires an active reservation held by the same uid, reusing the existing number_reservations TTL hold. The route was wired into index.ts as part of this issue - the agent that wrote purchaseVanity could not touch index.ts, leaving it unreachable dead code, the endpoint equivalent of a fake flag. Client: price shown as INR, insufficient_balance points at the web, and NO in-app top-up anywhere, because the app is read-only for money under this pivot.

success.why: THE MONEY ASSERTION. This value appearing means a user was charged and did not get a number. It is the failure the template tolerates and this implementation refunds, so it must never be observed.
Guards the fail-closed default. A purchase recorded at 0 tokens means avatokVanityNumberTokens was unset and the 503 guard was bypassed - i.e. paid numbers being given away free.

PIVOT-MKT-LANDING-1.description: Code half of making Marketplace the default landing screen. RootId.services is now FIRST in RootOrderPrefs.defaultOrder (root_order_store.dart) AND in the synchronous placeholder _root in shell_v2.dart - both were required; changing only one leaves a landing-race frame that briefly shows AvaTOK before the async load flips it. The persisted key was version-bumped shellv2_root_order_v1 -> _v2, WITHOUT WHICH THIS CHANGE IS INVISIBLE to every existing user: they have a stored order and would keep it forever. Verified the key goes through readScoped/scopedKey per-account helpers (mandatory in this codebase - one phone is shared by a parent and each child account) and that no other file referenced the old key. The three duplicated RootId->(icon,label) maps in app_switcher_bar.dart, app_order_screen.dart and shell_chrome.dart did NOT need edits: they are keyed lookups, not ordered lists. RootId.avaDial (AvaCalls) was deliberately left in place, now last - with Messenger calling killed it becomes an empty dialer, but its fate is an open question for the owner. NOT DONE and NOT SAFE YET: this ships behaviour-neutral because shellV2 defaults false. Flipping it is a whole-shell swap that has NEVER shipped to production, and it also requires marketplaceEnabled=true and avaAffiliateEnabled=false (or Affiliate hijacks the Services slot). Those are production KV flips for the owner, gated on a soak.

success.why: ShellV2 has never run in production, so the first thing to verify is that its roots mount and switch at all - before any claim about WHICH root leads.

Catches the version-bump failing. If users still land on AvaTOK and switch away from it, the persisted shellv2_root_order key was not actually reset and the old saved order is still winning - the exact way this change becomes invisible while looking shipped.

PIVOT-AI-SWITCHES-2.description: Build fix. [PIVOT-AI-SWITCHES-1] committed shell_v2.dart with an explicit FILE path, but another agent had uncommitted edits in that SAME file adding a PillMorseFooter reference. Passing a file path does NOT protect against a co-edited file, only against unrelated files - a sharper version of the directory-path sweeping lesson. main therefore referenced a widget whose definition (in core/ui/rajasthani_motifs.dart) was never committed, and CI run #627 failed the compile gate with 'shell_v2.dart:742:47: Not a constant expression'. This lands the PillMorseFooter definition so the reference resolves. Note flutter analyze passed LOCALLY throughout, because the local working tree had the uncommitted definition - only CI, building from committed code, could see it.
PIVOT-AI-SWITCHES-2.no_telemetry: Publishes an existing widget definition to unbreak the build; no gate, flag or behaviour change of its own. Verified by the check that matters: flutter test now compiles and passes 141/141.

SHELL-STATIC-BAR-1.description: Owner decision 2026-08-28: the ShellV2 footer bar becomes STATIC. Removed the expand/collapse handle, its caret and its 'Swipe up'/'Swipe down' pill; neither a tap nor a vertical drag does anything now. The app-switcher icon row is hidden behind a new compile-time const _kShowAppSwitcherIcons=false. A const rather than a RemoteConfig flag ON PURPOSE: with the handle gone there is no way for a user to reach the icon row, so a server flag that flipped it back on would render a row nobody could open and whose long-press reorder gestures are no longer discoverable. The slot builders and reorder machinery stay COMPILED but unreachable - the same keep-the-engine-remove-the-reachability approach used for the legacy Cloudflare call screen - so restoring the bar is a one-line change. The band keeps its 40px height because the RAJ-INDIGO-1 footer seam in shell_v2.dart pins itself to this bar's top edge.
SHELL-STATIC-BAR-1.no_telemetry: Presentation-only removal of an affordance, no gate, flag or new event. The contract is enforced by a source-text test instead: test/ui/app_type_scale_contract_test.dart asserts the 40px band height survives and that the swipe pill is gone.

SHELL-STATIC-BAR-2.description: Restates the app-menu contract test after [SHELL-STATIC-BAR-1]. The old test pinned the compact PILL treatment ('Swipe up' text, AD.bubbleOutPlay background, 12px type) which was deliberately removed. Following this test file's own stated convention - restate the contract rather than delete it - it now asserts the band's 40px height SURVIVES (the app-wide footer seam is positioned against it, so silently losing the height would move the seam on every screen), that the swipe labels are gone, and that the icon row remains gated off.
SHELL-STATIC-BAR-2.no_telemetry: Test-only. It exists so a future edit cannot silently restore the pill or drop the band height.

DESIGN-GUARD-ICONS-2.description: Follow-up to [DESIGN-GUARD-ICONS-1]. messenger_call_billing_ui_test.dart looked the HUD icon up by Icons.account_balance_wallet, which no longer exists there after the Phosphor migration. Updated to PhosphorIcons.wallet(PhosphorIconsStyle.regular). The assertion that matters is unchanged: the low-balance state tints the icon with AD.destructiveInk.
DESIGN-GUARD-ICONS-2.no_telemetry: Test-only; follows an icon rename. The behavioural assertion it guards is untouched.

SHELL-TEST-SEAM-1.description: Fixes a regression [PIVOT-MSGR-CALL-OFF-3] caused in test/call_accept_nonblocking_contract_test.dart. Those tests pin the hard-won [CALL-ACCEPT-FLASH-1] ordering contract - acceptRingingCall must request CallScreen BEFORE the human-accept claim resolves - traced from real PostHog data. RemoteConfig._cfg is empty in tests, so messengerCallingEnabled read its false default and the new gate refused before CallScreen was ever requested. Rather than weaken the assertions or change push_service.dart, added @visibleForTesting RemoteConfig.debugSetConfigForTest / debugResetConfigForTest and enabled the flag in setUp, so the ordering contract is genuinely exercised again - it still matters for the paid consultation lane, which shares the accept machinery. ALSO ADDED the missing test: with messengerCallingEnabled false, acceptRingingCall must NOT request CallScreen. That is the assertion whose absence let the kill switch land untested. The seam deliberately does not touch _cfgSig/revision, which exist to skip rebuilds on an unchanged poll; a test wants values live on the next getter read.
SHELL-TEST-SEAM-1.no_telemetry: Adds a test-only seam and test coverage; no production behaviour change. Verified by the suite: 141/141 pass, including the new flag-off assertion.

COMMERCIAL-TEST-GREEN-1.description: A REAL PRODUCTION CRASH, found while clearing the red build - and pre-existing, not caused by the pivot: CI runs #624, #625 and #626 had all failed this same test since 2026-08-25 with '139 tests passed, 1 failed', and nobody noticed. The last green build was #623, which is exactly why prod latestAppBuild sat at 10623. In _MySessionsScreenState (features/booking/commercial_customer_screens.dart), _tabs was a `late final TabController` initialised LAZILY. With both commercial flags off, build() renders the unavailable message instead of the TabBar, so nothing touches _tabs while the element is alive; the first access is _tabs.dispose() inside dispose(), which runs the lazy initialiser AT THAT MOMENT, constructing a TabController whose vsync does an inherited-widget lookup (TickerMode.getValuesNotifier) on an already-deactivating element - 'Looking up a deactivated widget's ancestor is unsafe'. Any real user opening My Sessions with commercial flags off and navigating away would hit it. Fixed by constructing the controller eagerly in initState() while the element is still active.

LIVE-CARVE-1.description: [LIVE-CARVE-1] Stop face-scanning creators without reopening the stranger-contact hole. gatePublicAction read ONE global boolean (identityGatingEnabled), so the only way to unblock listing creation was to ungate dm_stranger too - which config.ts DEFAULTS records as the confirmed CSAM-risk hole. Split PublicAction into CONTENT (post/listing/comment/live/group_post/group_create/upload/forward) and CONTACT (dm_stranger/call_stranger/group_join) via ONE Record<PublicAction,...> table so TypeScript refuses to compile an unclassified new variant, and added identityGateContentActionsEnabled (default true) which relaxes CONTENT only. CONTACT has no exemption path at all, by design. SECOND WALL ALSO REMOVED: publishListing gates live_event/consult on requireKyc, which reads kyc_status - a DIFFERENT table from identity_proofs - so relaxing liveness alone left every publish 403ing one step later; listingPublishKycRequired (default true) gates that, and FAILS CLOSED on an unreadable config (opposite posture to gatePublicAction, deliberately: an unreadable config must never be why an unverified account ships a paid listing). RESTORE BOTH FLAGS TO TRUE BEFORE REAL MONEY-IN.

success.note: The carve-out fired for listing creation - the owner's reported 403. Emitted at identity_gate.ts gatePublicAction only on the content-exempt branch, so absence means the flag did not land or KV still overrides it.

Proves the SECOND wall was cleared. requireKyc reads kyc_status, a different table from identity_proofs, so without this a draft is created and publish still 403s one step later - fixed-looking and still broken.

THE ASSERTION THAT MATTERS. This event must STILL FIRE for an unverified user messaging a stranger. Its absence means the carve-out gutted the stranger-contact gate instead of carving it - the difference between the change the owner asked for and reopening the hole config.ts DEFAULTS names as the confirmed CSAM risk. Verify by hand with an unverified test account if traffic is too low to assert.

COMM-CONSULT-ENT-1.description: [COMM-CONSULT-ENT-1] A paid 1:1 consult could not run, once, ever. commercialConsultJoin requires the creator to hold an entitlement with role='creator', and NOTHING in the repo ever wrote one - the only two INSERTs into commercial_entitlements were checkout's buyer row (viewer/buyer) and the live_event host self-grant. The expert was 403'd out of their own session, so creator x buyer overlap was zero, the two-party delivery check in commercial_settlement.ts failed, and the buyer's money parked in review_pending. Checkout now writes the creator row alongside the buyer's for consult_1to1 and verifies it to the same standard, aborting the checkout on a partial write rather than returning ok:true and failing at join time an hour later. SIDE EFFECT, INTENDED: the paid-extension path (commercial_stream_sessions.ts) asserts >=2 entitlements on the booking and could never see them, so every paid extension charged then auto-refunded; with the creator row it now passes. ALSO FIXED: entitlement() was role-BLIND (ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1 across all roles) with callers post-checking the role. Safe only while one account held at most one row per booking - which this change ends, since a creator booking their OWN consult now holds two rows differing only by role and stamped with the same created_at, making the old query return an arbitrary one and 409 intermittently. role is now a required FILTER on entitlement(); canViewSession keeps a separate, explicitly role-blind query because visibility is a different question from admission.

success.note: TWO distinct persons on one booking_id - the creator AND the buyer. min_events 2 is the point: one authorized join has always been possible (the buyer's), so asserting >=1 would have passed on the broken build. Ship-gate rule 2 applies: count DISTINCT persons on the newest build, not events.
FAILURE VALUE. entitlement_role_mismatch means the role filter and the written role disagree - most likely a creator who booked their own consult hitting the old non-deterministic lookup.

The end of the chain. A consult that ran produces a settled job, NOT review_pending. review_pending here means the two-party delivery evidence still is not being produced, i.e. one side still never joined.

FAILURE VALUE for the side effect. Every paid extension used to charge and auto-refund because the >=2 entitlement assertion could not pass. A reversed extension after this ships means the creator row is not being written.
